# Canon Clerk

> Canon Clerk combines an open specification for authored project rules (*canons*) with an automated, LLM-powered review gate (*clerk*) that audits pull requests against architectural invariants in CI.

Canon Clerk addresses the asymmetric cognitive tax placed on maintainers by AI code generators: generative coding tools accelerate code production, generating pull requests that pass static tests but quietly violate unwritten architectural tenets and project conventions. Canon Clerk formalizes these rules into zero-friction Markdown files stored in `.canons/` and audits changes using an efficient three-stage evaluation cascade.

Key architectural concepts:
- **Dual Pillars:** The project encompasses both the **Canon Standard** (an open specification for declarative, natural-language architectural invariants) and the **Clerk Runner** (the CI review gate and CLI engine that executes multi-stage LLM evaluation).
- **Core Platform:** Canon Clerk is an automated review engine and specification platform, not a shell utility or script collection; helper scripts in `.agents/skills/` are auxiliary automation tools for AI coding assistants.
- **Evaluation Cascade:** Audits execute across three stages—Stage 0 Deterministic Path Filter (0 tokens), Stage 1 Fast Screener (lightweight model), and Stage 2 Deep Auditor (frontier reasoning model).

## The Canon Standard

- [Canon Format Specification](SPEC.md): Complete normative grammar, metadata derivation rules (id, title, paths, inspect, tags, references), directive contracts (Guidance, Supplement, Rationale), and progressive disclosure tiers.
- [Dogfood Canons](.canons/): Internal project canons stored in the repository root illustrating real-world semantic rules enforced on this repository.
- [Canon Names Must State Invariants](.canons/canon-names-must-state-invariants.md): Reference canon requiring canon filenames to state testable invariants rather than passive categories.
- [Canons Must Be Atomic](.canons/canons-must-be-atomic.md): Reference canon requiring each canon file to address a single cohesive concept to prevent review flakiness.
- [Canons Must Be Falsifiable](.canons/canons-must-be-falsifiable.md): Reference canon requiring rules to codify objectively falsifiable criteria.
- [Canons Must Be Semantic](.canons/canons-must-be-semantic.md): Reference canon reserving canons for semantic invariants that cannot be validated deterministically with static linters.
- [Canon Lexicon Must Be Precise](.canons/canon-lexicon-must-be-precise.md): Reference canon requiring canons to employ precise domain and systems terminology rather than colloquial approximations.
- [Canon Directives Must Provide Distinct Signals](.canons/canon-directives-must-provide-distinct-signals.md): Reference canon requiring canon directives to supply distinct, non-redundant signal tailored to their target role.
- [Canon Content Must Be Succinct](.canons/canon-content-must-be-succinct.md): Reference canon requiring canon content to be dense, non-repetitive, and free from conversational filler.
- [Canon Rationales Must Be Self-Evident Or Explicit](.canons/canon-rationales-must-be-self-evident-or-explicit.md): Reference canon requiring invariant rationales to be self-evident or explicitly articulated via a Rationale directive.

## The Clerk Runner

- [Architecture & Evaluation Cascade](docs/architecture.md): Architectural specification of the three-stage evaluation cascade (Stage 0 Path Filter, Stage 1 Fast Screener, Stage 2 Deep Auditor) and the five-verdict matrix.
- [Clerk GitHub Action Configuration](README.md#2-add-to-github-actions): Example CI workflow configuration using pair-code/canon-clerk@v1 with screener and auditor models.
- [Clerk Quickstart & CLI Usage](README.md#quickstart): Setup guide, quickstart instructions, and GitHub Actions integration overview.

## Agent & Contributor Orientation

- [Agent Guidelines](AGENTS.md): Operational orientation, architectural anchors, and workspace navigation instructions for AI coding assistants.
- [Development Workflow](docs/development-workflow.md): Complete development guide covering issue claiming, triangular Git worktrees, Conventional Commit matrices, and pull request lifecycles.
- [Conventional Commit Reference](docs/conventional-commits.md): Normative Conventional Commit matrix, surface-to-prefix mapping, SemVer rules, and GitHub label taxonomy.
